finding.claim: Unauthenticated blind SQL injection: $_GET['sort'] is concatenated unvalidated into an ORDER BY clause and executed via PDO::query(), letting a remote client read arbitrary tables in app.db through row-ordering oracles.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' reads attacker-controlled input with no validation
String concatenation places the input directly into the ORDER BY clause of the SQL text
PDO::query() executes it; SQLite compiles only the first statement, so stacked writes are not reachable, but read subqueries are

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, cast, or quoting on the path; ?? 'id' is only a default; PDO cannot bind ORDER BY expressions as parameters; no authentication or authorization in the file, so the function is reachable by any caller if exposed. Not executed; conclusion based on code reading and SQLite ORDER BY semantics.

verdict.guard_found: none. There is no allowlist, cast, or quoting on the vulnerable path. list_users_sorted is never called in list.php (lines 2-18 only define it), and no other file exists in the directory to call it. list_users_safe (list.php:9-13) has an allowlist, but it is a separate function and not the one flagged.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (list.php:5 reads $_GET['sort'] unvalidated and list.php:6 concatenates it into the ORDER BY), but list.php:4-7 only defines list_users_sorted and nothing in the provided directory calls it, so an HTTP request to list.php just runs top-level code at lines 2-2 and never reaches the injectable query; the finding holds only if an external caller includes this file and invokes list_users_sorted with request input, which the code here does not show.

finding.claim: find_user() returns id and name for an arbitrary email with no authentication or authorization or rate limiting, creating an unauthenticated email-to-identity oracle for account enumeration and PII disclosure. The SQL itself is parameterized and not injectable.
finding.sink: Row lookup in find_user() returning id and name (list.php:16-18)

trace.note: Attacker-supplied email is bound as a parameter to execute()
fetch() returns the matching user's id and name to the caller

finding.guards_checked: Parameterized query (prevents SQL injection only); no session, role, or ownership check; no rate limiting in the file. Severity depends on how the function is wired into an application not present in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: none. The query at list.php:16 is a prepared statement with the email bound at list.php:17, which blocks SQL injection but is not an authorization or rate-limit control. Nothing in the repo checks session, role, or ownership before the fetch at list.php:18.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: list.php:17 binds $_GET['email'] and list.php:18 returns id and name, with no auth check in between. But find_user() is defined at list.php:15-19 and never called anywhere in this repo (the only file is list.php), so no HTTP request in the available code reaches it, and whether it is exposed depends on an application not present here.
